content.thinking:
I need to write the entire file in one pass without feedback, so I'm planning the design carefully to avoid errors: an Overwatch-style support cyborg medic around 1.75m tall, with white/pale armor panels over graphite undersuit and a cyan-teal glow accent, carrying a healing staff with a glowing cyan core ring.

Now I'm working out the skeleton layout—hips root near y≈0.95, spine chain running hips to chest to neck to head, arms in a slightly down T-pose, and legs below—while planning coordinate positions for each joint along the spine and chest chain to keep the rig readable and safe within the API's constraints.

I'm placing the neck, head, and jaw joints with specific world coordinates and direction vectors, treating head and jaw as individual joints with defined roles rather than chains, and linking the neck chain's parent to the spine's final joint to keep the hierarchy consistent.

For meshes, I'm planning helper functions like a box-builder that wraps primitive geometry with explicit bone attachment and placement options, aiming for a clean Overwatch-style look with crisp color blocking and toon shading.

I'll keep the palette mostly flat colors with a 64-color limit, using paints sparingly for panel lines and brushed-metal grain rather than relying on cel-shading throughout. For detail, I'm thinking of SVG decal textures for things like a chest emblem (a generic hex-with-plus shape to avoid logo issues), a staff panel, and the visor, then move into building the torso using a loft technique tied to the chest bone.

Writing loft station coordinates...

Given the lack of verification, I want to minimize exotic techniques and stick to simpler chain sweeps for the limbs instead.

Calculating arm joint positions...

Defining arm sweep radii...

Now for the legs: I'm setting hip joints at the pelvis sides, with thigh and shin lengths roughly reachable to the ankle target, adding a slight forward knee bend for a natural stance.

For the feet, I'm placing a boot box with a sole and toecap at the ankle position, sized to sit flush with the floor plane. I'm deciding the leg bone chain only needs hip-knee-ankle joints, skipping a separate toe joint for simplicity, and adding floor contact points at the base of each foot.

I'm working out the taper radii for the leg sweep from thigh to ankle, and planning armor shells—white cylindrical thigh plates, a sphere knee guard, and a tapered shin greave with an accent stripe over a dark undersuit. Now I'm placing the helmeted head with a visor, setting its position and ellipsoid skull proportions.

For the face, I'm deciding between a half-human/half-cybernetic look using skin tone versus a full helmet shell, and considering a partial sphere cap for the helmet that leaves the face exposed—tilting it back so it reads as an open-faced medic helmet rather than fully covering the front.

Adjusting the tilt to -50° so the front rim sits around brow level and the back rim drops near the base of the skull, giving it a hood-like helmet shape. I'll add a separate chin/jaw piece as a skin-toned shape beneath the cap.

For facial detail, I'm placing small eye shapes on the skull's front surface -- a dark organic eye on the left and a glowing cyan cybernetic eye on the right, positioning them symmetrically near the brow line.

Adding brow ridges, a nose wedge, a thin mouth line, and headset-style ear cups with cyan glow rings, plus a swept ponytail tucked under the helmet.

For the palette I'm settling on white/graphite armor with a single strong cyan accent for glow effects, dark brown hair, and warm skin tones to keep things from getting too busy with color.

Now I'm detailing the cyborg side: the right forearm as an exposed mechanical limb with segmented servo rings and cyan glow lines, paired with a cheek plate, cyber eye, and neck cabling.

I'm placing a staff in the left hand, defining its joint and shaft geometry so it runs vertically from the gripping hand down to the floor, with a wrapped grip near the hand and ornamental elements planned for the top and a spiked foot at the bottom.

Now I'm designing the staff head itself—a glowing orb nested inside a ring, with partial torus arcs forming crescent-like prongs above it.

Verifying the wing polygon doesn't self-intersect, then extruding it symmetrically on both sides with a slight bevel to form flat, mirrored wing shapes positioned near the shoulder, keeping them white with a glowing cyan edge.

Finishing the outline geometry, I'm now thinking about back equipment - a medical module backpack with glowing cyan canisters, a chest-mounted heal projector, hip pouches with med supplies, and white half-sphere shoulder pauldrons.

Still writing shoulder and chest armor geometry...

Now I'm planning an emblem texture plane for the chest, then building the torso as layered parts: a dark undersuit base, white chest armor, segmented abdomen plates, and a belt swept around the hips as a closed loop.

I'm working out the belt's closed catmull path points and tube radius, binding it to the hips bone for proper weighting, then sizing the torso loft radii at the hips using width and depth half-measures, with the sweep orientation set so binormal runs sideways and normal runs along the back. I'm also setting up a thin neck sweep in skin tone.

Now I'm adding a graphite cyber-collar ring with cyan trim at the neck base, then mapping out the bone hierarchy: spine chain joints named spine/chest/chestTip, a neck chain parented to chestTip ending in neckTip, and the head joint attached there. For the hands, I'm planning the left palm wrapping fingers around the staff and the right hand as an open robotic hand with extended segmented fingers.

Writing finger rig helper function...

Still working out finger coordinates...

Still placing palm and finger coordinates...

Finishing the thumb curve for the left hand, then setting up the mirrored right hand with an open, relaxed posture—wrist, palm box, and finger joints positioned with a slight downward-forward bend.

For materials, I'm distinguishing the two sides: the left arm stays human but suited, with a graphite glove and a lighter plate on the back of the hand, while the right arm is fully robotic—exposed grey metal forearm with cyan glowing seams and joint rings, and metal-segmented fingers to match. Now I'm setting up the finger bone chains to parent correctly to the wrist joint tip.

I'm defining each finger as its own named joint chain with digit roles, using unique index-based names, and treating each short polyline as a two-span chain for the sweep geometry. For the sweep itself I'm tapering the radius along each finger with rounded caps so the joints read as smooth, slightly fillet-rounded segments.

For hair, I'm sketching a ponytail as a catmull curve of a few points trailing down and back from the head, tapering its radius from thick near the scalp to thin at the tip, but I need to adjust its starting point so it emerges from a gap at the rear of the helmet shell rather than clipping through it.

I'm also working out the helmet's tilt rotation around the X axis, checking that rotating by -50 degrees about the head's own center correctly swings the top of the cap backward as intended.

Checking the front rim coverage, the forward direction sits right at the rim edge around 110-111 degrees of polar angle from the tilted axis, meaning the cap just barely covers the forehead at roughly 30 degrees of elevation, while the straight-ahead eye-level direction falls just outside.

Working through the rest of the body - top, back, and back-bottom directions all land within the covered polar range, so the helmet covers down to about -45 degrees elevation at the back, resembling a hood. Side directions near the ears also fall within the covered zone.

Now I'm checking the helmet's scale relative to the skull - the helmet ellipsoid is scaled up proportionally larger than the skull in each axis to leave a margin, and I need to confirm whether that scaling is applied in local space before the rotation is applied.

I'm settling on a near-spherical helmet scale that's at least as large as the skull's maximum extent plus a small margin on each side, keeping the same center point so the helmet reads as fitted armor.

Now I'm planning additional details: a cyan visor stripe, a crest fin on top with a cyan accent, side headset cylinders near the ears with a glowing ring, and a cyborg-style cheek plate with a glowing eye and line detail on one side of the face. I'm also working out the nose geometry as a small box placed just below the forehead area.

For the mouth, I'm calculating where the jaw ellipsoid surface sits at different y-levels so the jawline and mouth placement line up properly with the skull's front curvature, then positioning a thin dark box as the mouth line at that calculated depth.

Now I'm working out eye placement: the sclera ellipsoid needs to sit on the skull surface at the right x/y offset, with the iris sphere protruding slightly further forward so it's visible past the sclera, and a small dark pupil sphere nested just in front of that.

Giving the left eye a brown iris and the right eye a cyberpunk cyan-glowing iris with a ring, then adding dark brow boxes above each. For the neck I'm sketching a couple of thin cable sweeps running from the jaw down toward the collar, trying to decide whether to attach them to the head or neck bone for proper deformation.

Now I'm planning the chest armor: a plate with a glowing cyan emblem decal, shoulder straps, ab segments, a sternum core ring, and a back pack. For the emblem texture I'm designing a hexagon-and-plus SVG icon with a dark graphite backing and cyan stroke/accent colors to mount on the chest plate.

I'm also considering a brushed-metal mottle paint texture for the armor panel surfaces to add subtle seam and highlight variation.

For accent details, I'm thinking of thin glowing cyan chevron plates extruded onto the shins, plus maybe a small decal marking on the thigh.

I'll add two more texture ideas: a hex-plus emblem and some tech barcode-style striping on the forearm plate, applied as a flat plane over the robotic arm. Part count is staying moderate at around 250 with low triangle count, so I'm ready to start composing the actual geometry.

Setting up imports from the builder, path, ik, paint, and texture modules, careful to only pull in what's actually used so I don't trip unused-import errors. Then I'm defining the meta object with name, description, style, and commit hash, followed by starting the color palette with white tones.

I'll add a small warm amber accent sparingly, maybe four pieces, alongside the cyan for indicator lights. For the armor material, I'm defining a mottled white paint pattern with subtle contrast variation to break up flat surfaces.

Now I'm setting up the builder instance and a vector helper, then writing a segment-drawing utility that takes two points, radii, color, and bone reference to construct limb geometry. I'm also sorting out the type for color fills, using a union of string or Paint type pulled from the paint module rather than importing something incompatible.

For the segment helper, I switch to using `fromArray` since spreading a number array into the Vector3 constructor causes a type error, then compute the cylinder's length and orientation between the two points, aiming it along the direction vector. I'm also building a box helper for rigid parts, handling the optional rotation parameter carefully since strict optional property typing might reject explicit undefined values.

I define a generic part-building function `P` that assembles a `PartOptions` object conditionally, only adding rotation and scale when provided, and checking that the scale type (number or vector-like array) and bone type align with what `b.part` expects. I also sketch a sphere helper using a low-poly `SphereGeometry`.

Now I'm starting to lay out the skeleton itself, defining the hips as the root joint with a spine role, then beginning the spine chain running upward from the pelvis.

I'm defining the spine chain with explicit joint names and parenting it to the hips, noting the joint names override the default chain naming. I'm then parenting leg chains to hips with hip/knee/ankle names, and working through how the `limb` helper takes root/target positions, segment lengths, and bend direction vectors to compute IK-style joint placement, verifying the reach distance against the limb segment lengths to make sure the pose is achievable.

I'm checking boot and shin geometry alignment at the ankle — making sure the sole, foot box, and boot shaft cylinder dimensions line up with where the ankle joint sits, then working out the contact point array and confirming the leg chain's three joints (hip, knee, ankle tip) correctly map to thigh, shin, and foot bones.

Now I'm defining the sweep radii across the leg and layering armor plates onto the thigh bone, computing lerp points between hip and knee to position a slightly larger-radius cylinder over the undersuit mesh.

I'll skip the front plate box idea and instead add cyan torus rings oriented along the bone direction using the axis option, plus a knee guard sphere offset forward with a matching ring accent.

Adding shin front plate geometry...

Boots get a graphite base with a white toe cap and dark steel sole, plus a small glowing cyan strip along the side. For the pelvis I'm placing hip armor boxes on either side of the hip bones.

Then I'm adding a belt with pouches, cylindrical medical canisters with glowing cyan caps, and a layered tabard/skirt plate hanging in front with a rear tail plate. I'm also giving the character a syringe-style injector on a left thigh holster, plus a backpack mounted to the chest/back bone.

Now I'm detailing the backpack unit itself with glowing vents and twin canisters, then moving to the shoulders—adding a pauldron dome over the left shoulder joint with a cyan stripe ring, and a smaller, more mechanical pauldron with exposed pistons on the right to give that arm a cybernetic look. I'm continuing into the upper arm armor with a graphite sleeve and a short white bicep band.

Writing arm geometry...

Checking the right hand's fingers hang downward with the palm facing inward, and confirming the left hand grips the staff at the mirrored x position. I'm verifying the joint naming convention for each arm chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist with side suffix) and setting the sweep radii for the left arm.

Defining chest armor as a lofted shell layered over the undersuit, with stations spaced along the torso and a slight forward z-offset to give the plates volume.

Adding abdominal plate positions...

I realize I can decal the emblem onto the chest loft surface directly using a point and direction to project it onto the curved shape, which should sit naturally rather than floating. I could also extend decals to the pauldron spheres for additional detailing like a stripe.

Checking the neck-to-head chain positioning, I confirm the head sphere sits properly above the neck, giving a total height around 1.8m which feels reasonable for a medic figure. Now I'm adding ear details, planning to tuck small cylindrical earcups under the helmet rim on each side.

Working out the cyborg headset boom mic curve from the earcup toward the cheek, then placing a steel cheek plate ellipsoid scaled and positioned to fit against the skull's contour on the right side of the face.

Still computing head geometry...

Placing a thin glowing cyan torus around the rim to act as a light stripe, computing its offset along the cap's axis so it sits right at the brim edge with a full ring all the way around. Now thinking about adding a top fin detail to the helmet as well.

Shaping the fin into a simple non-crossing polygon with cyan glow, embedded slightly into the dome. I'll skip detailed neck cables, add a couple simple ones, and move on to building the staff bone joint structure.

Now I'm defining the staff geometry: a tapered shaft running through the gripped hand, a grip section with cyan torus rings, and a tapered cone foot at the bottom for the stand.

Continuing the staff build, I'm adding the lower white and steel sleeve segments with cyan glow grooves, the upper shaft with a white collar and glowing ring, and finishing with a flared head mount topped by a cyan orb.

Checking wing extents won't collide with the shoulder pauldron or body, keeping clearance near x=.22. I'm also considering small cyan glow points for the orb, maybe a decal on the staff grip, and whether to add a hip-mounted caduceus holster for extra detail.

Now I'm double-checking the glow logic—making sure glowing parts use flat color strings rather than the shared Paint material, verifying that sweep, frustum box, and decal functions all return proper Part/Sweep objects, and scanning for other runtime pitfalls like loft stations and bone chain setup.

Then I'm designing the emblem SVG as a hexagonal badge with a cyan cross motif, and starting the tech-panel SVG for the forearm with thin horizontal bars and tick marks. Writing SVG code...

I'm also considering a subtle carbon-weave grain texture for the undersuit material, generated with a noise function along one axis.

Now I'm sizing a 1024 paint sheet for roughly 6 square meters of painted surface, working out that gives about 3mm per texel, which is fine. I'm planning separate paints for armor mottling, suit grain, and boots, and considering a custom panel-line paint that overlays thin horizontal lines on the armor base using a fractional modulo check on the y-coordinate.

I decide the panel-line approach creates odd uniform seams everywhere, so I'll skip it and handle seams through geometry instead. Now I'm writing the actual build function, starting with color constants and the skeleton structure -- defining the hips joint, a spine chain with three joints (spine1, chest, chestTip), and then a neck chain parented off the chest tip.

Writing head, jaw, and arm joint hierarchy...

Setting up vector helpers for interpolating between points along the arm segments...

Still writing arm segments...

I'm checking the pauldron dome placement against the chest shell geometry — the dome's inner radius at x=.135 overlaps the torso's chest shell, which spans down to about .17 at that shoulder height, so I need to adjust the offset or scale to avoid clipping.

Now I'm computing the tilted rim orientation for the pauldron's cyan trim ring, rotating the vertical axis by the shoulder angle to find where the ring plane should sit relative to the dome.

Then I'm turning to the right (cyborg) side's smaller pauldron sphere and shoulder joint, planning the steel ball and graphite torus rings that make up its mechanical upper arm.

Still adding forearm details...

I want the plate thin along X and extended along Z, positioning its outer face just past the arm's surface, and computing the tech decal position along the forearm accordingly. I'll handle hands separately through a dedicated function taking scale, wrist joint, and cyborg parameters.

Now I'm laying out the right hand: a steel palm box parented to the wrist joint, plus a white back plate positioned outward on the lateral side. For fingers, I'm setting up a loop to compute evenly spaced x-offsets across the palm width for each of the four finger chains.

Working out finger joint positions by segment length...

Working out the left hand's grip around the staff, checking that the shaft position and finger curl coordinates overlap correctly with the palm so the fingers wrap convincingly around the shaft without clipping through it.

Now I'm positioning the thumb so it wraps from the opposite side compared to the fingers, checking the coordinates don't overlap finger tips. Then I'll move on to the boots, chain details, and consider adding small rivet spheres around the wrists for extra texture.

Now I'm setting up the module imports needed for the build—pulling in the builder, IK limb helper, catmull spline for ponytail/cables/belt, paint and texture utilities, and core skeleton types—then defining helper types for color and point inputs before starting the construction function.

Writing geometry helpers...

Writing torso loft code...

Checking the hip-to-leg transition width so the pelvis station lines up smoothly with the leg radius without creating visible seams.

Making the belt steel-colored with a white buckle box up front, and checking that the belt radius clears the pelvis loft at that station so it doesn't clip. Now I'm sketching waist armor plates to add as a lower skirt layer.

I'm fleshing out the torso details: a glowing sternum ring, a chest emblem decal, and considering cyan glow bars or heal-port plates on the upper chest sides, though some of these I decide to skip for simplicity. I'm also considering a small backpack box mounted on the back of the chest shell near the shoulder line.

I'm placing the backpack with side canisters, cyan glow cores, and a decal centered between them, carefully positioning depths so nothing clips through the back plate, and now starting to sketch out the hose connections.

For the legs, I'm building the boot geometry: a steel sole, an armored boot body, and a toe cap using a scaled sphere, with pieces stacked and offset in y to form a convincing foot shape on the ankle joint bone.

I'm adding the ankle shroud as a tapered cylinder segment and a cyan strip ring to accent the shin-to-boot transition, keeping the shroud rigid on the foot bone so it reads correctly as the leg bends. Next I'll move up to the knee plate on the second joint.

Still positioning holster geometry...

I'm thinking about giving the cyborg medic some asymmetric robotic detailing — exposed pistons and a cyan glow strip on the right leg while keeping the left leg fully armored for contrast, plus a hanging loincloth/tabard plate at the hips.

Now I'm placing the hair, positioning a ponytail that sweeps behind the head and neck using a curved path with tapering width, making sure it passes near the backpack without clipping through it.

Placing the hair tie ring using the tail path's position and tangent at t=.3 for orientation, sizing it small with a thin tube. Then adding neck cables as a tapered sweep along a curve from the base of the neck downward, with a secondary thin sheath for detail.

Now building the collar as a cylinder segment around the chest, with a glowing cyan ring near the neck base and a steel cyber plate on one side. The jaw gets a scaled sphere for shape, plus a smaller scaled steel ball layered on as a cyber plate, and I'm starting on the mouth as a small flattened box.

I'm continuing with the skull sphere underneath, then layering a sliced sphere geometry on top as the helmet cap, angled and scaled to fit the head -- the open bottom of that cap geometry means the skull is only visible through the rim opening, which should look fine visually.

Now I'm positioning a thin glowing ring at the rim of the cap, computing its tilted axis and center offset so it sits correctly against the ellipsoid's nonuniform scaling -- working through the radius math for how the ring wraps around that tilted opening.

Next I'm moving to the helmet's ear cups, defining them as cylinder segments positioned on either cheek, with an inner recessed piece slightly offset for depth.

Now I'm adding details like a thin steel antenna rod on the left ear cup angling upward and back, with a glowing ball tip, plus a cyber scanner torus lens for the right eye monocle.

For the pelvis I need hip joints feeding into the leg bones. I'm writing a loop that builds each leg chain per side, computing hip/knee/ankle positions symmetrically and attaching them to the hips parent with contact points defined.

Readonly number arrays should accept fine as rotation inputs. I'm checking whether joints array indexing could trigger strict null checks with noUncheckedIndexedAccess, but since the api examples rely on direct indexing like spine.joints[0], it should be safe to follow that pattern. Time to write the full file now, keeping it compact.

Writing finger sweep helper...

Still writing hand and thumb coordinates...

I'm keeping the color palette compact, well under the limit, and double-checking the emblem decal placement on the chest geometry before finalizing.

Now I'm setting up the back decal position and direction, and configuring the tech plane geometry with its texture mapping on the arm bone.
